title: Lateral (Euler) buckling load of whole ligamentous lumbar spines under vertical load - intact

quantity.name: buckling load
quantity.definition: vertical axial load at which at least one vertebra rotated > 1.2 deg in the frontal plane (upper bound; per specimen and group average, no SD)

source.authors: Crisco JJ, Panjabi MM, Yamamoto I, Oxland TR
source.sample: 6 fresh-frozen ligamentous lumbar spines (3 L2-S1, 3 L1-S1); human cadaver whole lumbar spines, muscles removed

protocol.summary: Sacrum and most superior vertebra cast in polyester resin; specimen oriented with L4 superior endplate horizontal. Vertical axial dead-weight load applied to the superior vertebra (via loading jig, counterweights cancel jig/mounting weight), increased in 20 or 40 N steps, 30 s hold per step; superior vertebra free to move in the frontal plane but restrained in anterior-posterior translation by linear bearings (sagittal buckling prevented). Frontal-plane rotations of each vertebra by stereophoto/radiogrammetry. Buckling load = load at which at least one vertebra rotated > 1.2 deg (upper bound, discrete steps). Conditions in order: intact (INT), L5-S1 disc injury (DISC), plus removal of L5 inferior facets (FAC).
how_to_simulate: Model ligamentous L1-S1 (or L2-S1); fix sacrum; orient so the L4 superior endplate is horizontal
Apply a vertical (non-follower) compressive dead load to the superior vertebra; let the top vertebra translate/rotate freely in the frontal plane but block anterior-posterior translation
Increase load in 20-40 N steps; find the load at which any vertebra rotates > 1.2 deg laterally (buckling); report frontal-plane rotations after buckling
Repeat after L5-S1 disc injury and after removing the L5 inferior facets (injury details in Crisco 1992 Part I)
protocol.notes: Buckling loads are upper bounds (discrete dead-weight steps). Specimen 5 has no intact value. Postbuckling rotation definition: frontal-plane rotation theta_k of vertebra Lk as reported in Tables 4-6 (relative vertebral rotation; theta_5 is L5 on S1).

extraction.uncertainty: loads are discrete dead-weight steps (20-40 N), values are upper bounds
extraction.check_notes: Re-read Tables 1 and 2 from the page image (OCR garbled Table 2): specimen 5 INT '-', DISC 78, FAC 39; averages 88/59/39 (L1-S1) and 98/72/26 (L2-S1) match recomputed means; Table 3 experiment column 88/59/39 matches.

pass_rule.rule: model buckling load (vertical load, frontal plane) within [min,max] of specimens of the same length; and << follower-load capacity (Patwardhan)
